channel.title: Templates on Best of AI
channel.description: Recent content in Templates on Best of AI

item.title: Apify
item.description: Apify turns the web into a source of structured data. A marketplace called Apify Store offers thousands of Actors, which are cloud programs that scrape or automate specific websites and tasks: extracting listings from Google Maps, posts from social networks, product details from e-commerce sites, or contact information from pages. You configure an Actor, run it in the cloud, and receive results as JSON, CSV, or through an API, without managing servers or proxies.

item.title: Azure AI Document Intelligence
item.description: Azure AI Document Intelligence reads documents so applications can use the data. Its layout model finds text, tables, headings, and selection marks, and prebuilt models recognize common document types such as invoices, receipts, business cards, identity documents, and many tax and mortgage forms, returning fields like totals, dates, and names with confidence scores. You can train custom models with a small number of examples to extract the fields in your own forms.

item.title: Cartoon Animator
item.description:
Cartoon Animator is built to make 2D animation approachable. You can bring in artwork, a photo, or one of the included characters, add a bone rig, and animate the character. Face tracking from a webcam drives expressions, motion templates provide walks and gestures, and audio can generate lip movement automatically.

The software includes tools for composing scenes, with backgrounds, props, and cameras, and it can export videos, image sequences, and assets for editors. It also links to Reallusion’s other products. Users can bring in layered files from Photoshop and Clip Studio, which helps artists who draw their own characters.

item.title: Clipchamp
item.description:
Clipchamp is designed for people who need a video without learning professional software. The editor has a drag and drop timeline, trimming and filters, text, transitions, and a library of templates for social posts, ads, and presentations. It records your screen and webcam, so it handles tutorials and quick explainers.

AI features speed up common tasks. Auto Compose builds a draft video from clips and photos, captions are generated automatically, text to speech adds narration, and silence removal tightens recordings. Microsoft folded the tool into its ecosystem, so it integrates with OneDrive and Microsoft 365, and a version of the editor ships with Windows.

item.title: Constant Contact
item.description:
Constant Contact has been a staple of small business email marketing for a long time. Users build mailing lists, design emails from templates with a drag-and-drop editor, schedule campaigns, and track opens and clicks. It emphasizes ease of use and customer support, including phone and chat help, which appeals to owners who are not marketing specialists.

The product extends beyond email. Tools include SMS marketing, social media posting, landing pages, online surveys, and event registration, with automation for welcome series and follow-ups. AI features generate email copy and subject lines, suggest content ideas, and help build campaigns from a short brief, and an AI-driven website builder is part of the suite.

item.title: Mentimeter
item.description:
Mentimeter makes presentations interactive. You build slides with questions such as multiple choice polls, word clouds, rating scales, rankings, and open-ended questions, share a join code or QR code, and the audience responds from their phones. Results appear live on the screen, which turns a one-way talk into a conversation and gives quiet participants an easy way to contribute.

It suits a range of settings. Teachers use it to check understanding, trainers to energize workshops, and companies to run all-hands meetings and collect anonymous feedback. Features include quizzes with leaderboards, Q&A with upvoting, and templates, and you can import existing slides from PowerPoint or Google Slides. AI helps generate a presentation from a prompt, suggest questions, and summarize responses.

item.title: MURAL
item.description:
MURAL gives distributed teams a shared canvas. Participants add sticky notes, diagrams, images, and text to a large board at the same time, and facilitators run sessions with tools such as timers, private mode for individual thinking, voting, and guided agendas. A big library of templates covers retros, roadmaps, design sprints, and strategy exercises.

AI assists with the messy part of workshops, which is making sense of dozens of notes. It can group sticky notes by theme, summarize a board, and generate ideas to get a session started. Integrations with Microsoft Teams, Zoom, Jira, and Slack connect boards to the tools where work gets done.

item.title: Prezi
item.description:
Prezi stands out for its zooming interface. Instead of a linear deck, you lay out ideas spatially on a big canvas and the presentation moves among them with motion, which gives viewers a sense of how topics relate and can make a talk feel more dynamic. The approach suits overview-and-detail stories and keeps attention better for some audiences than traditional slides.

The product line has expanded. Prezi Video overlays presentation content next to the speaker on video calls and recordings, Prezi Design creates interactive visual content, and the AI assistant generates presentations from a prompt, rewrites text, and builds structure. Templates, brand kits, and analytics help teams use it for sales, teaching, and training.

item.title: Rocket Lawyer
item.description:
Rocket Lawyer is aimed at people who need legal help without a full law firm engagement. Members answer questions in an interview format and the service generates documents such as lease agreements, NDAs, wills, and operating agreements. Documents can be signed electronically and stored, and templates are tailored to the user’s state.

Beyond documents, membership gives access to attorneys through ask-a-lawyer services and, for some matters, discounted consultations. Small businesses use it for formation, contracts, and compliance support. AI tools help explain legal terms and draft documents, and are positioned as a way to get started before consulting a professional.

item.title: Squarespace
item.description:
Squarespace appeals to people who want an attractive site without a developer. You choose a template, change the content with a visual editor, and publish with hosting, security, and a domain included. Its designs are known for clean layouts and good typography, which makes it popular with creatives, small businesses, restaurants, and portfolio sites.

The platform goes beyond static pages. Built-in commerce handles products, subscriptions, and checkout, email campaigns support marketing, and Acuity Scheduling covers appointments. AI features include a site builder that generates a starting design and content from answers to a few questions, text-writing assistance, and tools for improving search visibility. Analytics show traffic and sales.

item.title: WordPress
item.description:
WordPress is the software behind a large share of the web. You install it on a web host or sign up with a hosted service, and manage pages, posts, media, and users from a dashboard. A block editor lets you build layouts visually, and thousands of themes control how a site looks. Plugins extend it for SEO, contact forms, memberships, caching, analytics, and online stores through WooCommerce.

It comes in two forms that are easy to confuse. WordPress.org is the free software you host yourself, which gives full control and requires handling hosting, updates, and security. WordPress.com is a hosted service from Automattic with plans that handle those chores. AI arrives mostly through add-ons: Jetpack and other plugins offer writing help, image generation, and chat assistants, and AI site builders can generate a first draft of a site from a prompt. The core project is also adding building blocks for AI features.

item.title: TypingMind
item.description:
TypingMind is a front end for AI models. A user supplies API keys, and gets a clean chat app with conversation folders, prompt libraries, and tools. Pay-per-use API pricing can be cheaper than several subscriptions, especially for light users.

Features include support for multiple models in one place, custom assistants, plugins, and knowledge uploads, and teams can share setups with controlled access. It is a paid product with a one-time or subscription license depending on the plan.

item.title: Claude Slides
item.description:
Claude Slides makes decks from a conversation. You describe the audience and the point of the presentation, share notes or source files, and Claude produces a set of slides with an outline, text, and layout. You can then ask for changes, such as a different order, a tighter message, or new visuals, and edit individual slides directly.

The finished deck can be presented from within Claude or exported to PowerPoint or PDF for use elsewhere. Because it lives in the same place as the conversation, you can pull information from uploaded documents and revise based on feedback without switching tools. It sits alongside Claude’s other creation features, including Docs.

item.title: Igly
item.description:
Igly focuses on product images. A seller uploads photos of items, and the tool removes or replaces backgrounds, places products in lifestyle scenes, adjusts lighting, and creates variations for marketplaces. An infinite canvas lets users arrange and edit many images in one project.

Agents handle multi-step edits from a plain description, such as producing a set of listing images in a consistent style. Presets match the dimensions and rules of common platforms. Sellers use it to reduce the cost of photography and design.

item.title: Enhancv
item.description:
Enhancv guides people through writing a resume. A user chooses a template, fills in experience, and gets prompts and suggestions on wording, such as adding numbers to show results and avoiding vague phrases. A content analyzer scores the draft and points out weak areas.

Templates are designed to be readable by applicant tracking systems, and sections can be customized for different roles. Additional tools include cover letter help, a resume checker, and a personal website option. AI features suggest bullet points and rewrite text, which can save time when starting from scratch.

item.title: Hocoos
item.description:
Hocoos aims at people who want a website without a design process. The user answers questions about their business and style, and the AI generates pages, text, and images, and sets up features such as contact forms, an online store, or appointment booking. An editor allows changes afterward.

The platform includes hosting, a domain option, and SEO basics, plus marketing helpers such as email tools and social media content. It is positioned for small and local businesses and solo entrepreneurs who need an online presence quickly.

item.title: Palette.fm
item.description:
Palette.fm adds color to old photos. A user uploads a black-and-white image, and the AI predicts plausible colors for skin, clothing, sky, and objects, returning a colorized version in seconds. Different style options change the overall palette, and results can be refined.

Families use it for old portraits, and historians and archivists use it to make collections more engaging. Colorization is an educated guess based on learned patterns, so colors may not match the real scene, and it should not be presented as historically accurate.

item.title: Heidi Health
item.description:
Heidi is an AI scribe for clinicians. During a visit, with the patient’s consent, it records and transcribes the conversation, then generates a note in the structure the clinician prefers, such as SOAP or a specialty template. The clinician reviews and edits before saving it to the record.

Beyond notes, it can write letters, patient instructions, and other documents from the same consultation, and supports multiple languages. Heidi began in Australia and has grown internationally, with a free tier that made it popular with individual practitioners alongside plans for clinics and health systems.

item.title: Creately
item.description:
Creately combines diagramming and whiteboarding in one workspace. You can draw flowcharts, org charts, mind maps, UML diagrams, process maps, wireframes, and more using shape libraries and templates, then connect them with smart connectors that stay attached when you move things. An infinite canvas supports brainstorming and planning, and teams can edit together in real time with comments and cursors.

Some features go beyond plain drawing. Diagrams can be linked to data, so a shape can show information from a spreadsheet or tool, and cards and tables let you build lightweight planning boards. AI features generate a diagram from a text description, summarize or expand notes, and suggest ideas for brainstorming. Presentations and exports in common formats help you share work, and integrations connect with Slack, Confluence, Google Workspace, and Microsoft Teams.

item.title: FlowGPT
item.description:
FlowGPT started as a place to share ChatGPT prompts. People post prompts for writing, coding, productivity, roleplay, and other uses, and others can browse by category, upvote the best, and copy them. Over time it added the ability to run prompts directly on the site and to build small chatbot-style apps, so a prompt can become a reusable tool.

The community aspect drives it. Creators gain followers and recognition for popular prompts, and the site hosts character chats and templates for tasks such as resume writing or SEO. It offers a way to learn prompting techniques by examining what others have written. Many of the contributions are playful or experimental, with quality that varies.

item.title: XMind
item.description:
XMind is a long-standing mind mapping tool known for its range of layouts. Start with a central idea and branch outward, or switch to another structure such as a logic chart, fishbone diagram, matrix, tree chart, or timeline to fit the problem. It has a polished interface, attractive themes, and features such as markers, stickers, notes, and attachments, and it works offline.

Special modes help with presentation and organization. Brainstorming mode captures ideas quickly, outline view turns a map into a list, and Zen mode removes distractions. A presentation feature plays the map as a slideshow, and exports cover PDF, images, Word, and Markdown. AI features can generate a map from a topic, expand a branch with suggestions, and summarize content into a structure.

item.title: 10Web
item.description:
10Web combines site generation with hosting. You describe a business or enter the address of an existing website, and the AI builds a WordPress site with layout, text, and images, which you can then edit with a visual builder based on Elementor. The result is a standard WordPress site, so it can use the plugin and theme ecosystem and can be moved elsewhere.

Hosting and optimization are part of the package. Sites run on managed WordPress hosting with a focus on speed, including automatic optimization of images and code to improve page speed scores, and tools for backups and security. AI features generate copy, images, and SEO suggestions, and an assistant can edit pages based on instructions. Agencies can white-label the platform and manage client sites, and there is an API for builders who want to embed it.

item.title: Beautiful.ai
item.description:
Beautiful.ai tackles a common complaint about PowerPoint: you spend more time fiddling with alignment than thinking about content. Its slides are built from smart templates that rearrange themselves when you add or remove text, images, or chart elements, so the design stays clean. Rules keep spacing, fonts, and colors consistent, and a library of layouts covers timelines, comparisons, charts, team slides, and more.

AI features help create the first draft. You can describe a presentation, or paste in notes, and it generates an outline and slides in the app’s format, which you then edit. Teams can store brand colors, fonts, and logos in a shared theme, share slide libraries, and collaborate on decks with comments. Presentations can be exported to PowerPoint or PDF, or shared by link with view analytics.

item.title: BeFunky
item.description:
BeFunky is a browser-based editor for people who want quick results without learning Photoshop. The photo editor has sliders for exposure and color, crop and resize tools, and a large set of filters and effects. A collage maker arranges photos into layouts, and the graphic designer tool offers templates for social media posts, flyers, and cards. Everything runs in a web page, with mobile access too.

AI tools handle common edits. An enhancer sharpens and improves photos, a background remover cuts out subjects, and retouching tools smooth skin and remove blemishes. Artistic effects turn photos into paintings or cartoons, and an upscaler increases resolution. Newer features add AI image generation and a way to remove objects. Many of these are one-click operations, which is the main appeal.

item.title: CharlieHR
item.description:
CharlieHR is designed for companies without a dedicated HR team. It keeps employee records, tracks time off, runs onboarding checklists, stores contracts, and supports regular reviews and one-on-ones. The interface is simple, so small teams can adopt it without lengthy setup.

An AI assistant helps with everyday HR questions about policies and employment topics, and supports tasks such as drafting job descriptions or other documents. Integrations connect with payroll providers, so data does not need to be entered twice. Reports give founders a view of headcount and absence.

item.title: Chibi AI
item.description:
Chibi AI aims to support writers who produce longer pieces. It provides a clean editor where you can draft with AI help, continue a passage, rewrite sections, and adjust tone or length, with a focus on staying in the flow of writing instead of juggling templates. The tool is aimed at bloggers, students, and fiction writers who want a collaborator that suggests next paragraphs or alternative phrasing.

It offers features common to AI writing tools, such as outline generation, summarizing, expanding ideas, and fixing grammar, with options to guide the style. Users can save projects and export their writing. The simple interface keeps focus on the text instead of a long menu of tools.

item.title: Copy.ai
item.description:
Copy.ai began as one of the first popular AI copywriting tools. Users choose a template or write a prompt, and the tool generates headlines, product descriptions, email sequences, ads, and social captions. A brand voice feature helps keep the tone consistent.

The product later shifted toward workflows for go-to-market teams. Marketers and sales teams can chain steps that research accounts, draft outreach, and produce content at scale, using multiple language models. Chat and knowledge features let the AI draw on company information.

item.title: Copy.ai
item.description:
Copy.ai started in the first wave of AI writing tools. You picked a template, such as a product description, email, or social caption, answered a few prompts, and got several drafts to edit. It was popular with marketers and small businesses who needed a lot of copy quickly. Over time it moved away from one-off text generation and toward automating sales and marketing processes.

Its later product centered on workflows. A team could chain steps together, for example researching an account, pulling in data, drafting outreach, and writing a CRM update, and let AI agents run the sequence on a schedule or trigger. A data layer called Tables kept the inputs organized, and the aim was to replace manual go-to-market busywork with repeatable automations rather than just generating paragraphs.

item.title: Decktopus
item.description: Decktopus is built for people who need a presentation quickly. You enter a topic or a short brief, answer a few questions about the audience and goal, and the AI produces an outline and a deck of designed slides with suggested images and speaker notes. You then edit the text and layout in a drag-and-drop editor. It also offers templates for pitches, reports, and sales decks, and a brand kit for colors and logos.

item.title: Durable
item.description:
Durable promises a website with minimal effort. You tell it the kind of business you run and where you are, and it builds a site with pages, copy, images, and a layout in under a minute, which you can then edit with simple controls. It’s aimed at freelancers and local service businesses, such as plumbers, photographers, and consultants, who need an online presence quickly.

Beyond the site, Durable includes small-business tools. A built-in CRM tracks leads and customers, an invoicing feature handles billing, and AI assistants help write blog posts, social content, and marketing copy. It offers hosting and a custom domain, and basic analytics. Everything lives in one account, so owners avoid piecing together several services.

item.title: FlexClip
item.description:
FlexClip is a browser-based video maker for people without editing experience. You start from a template or a blank timeline, drop in clips, images, text, and music from its stock library, and trim and arrange them with drag and drop. It exports in common formats and sizes for social platforms, and includes screen and webcam recording for tutorials. It is used by small businesses, teachers, and social media managers.

AI features speed up production. Text-to-video builds a draft from a script or idea, an AI script writer drafts the narration, and auto subtitles transcribe speech and add captions in many languages. Background removal for video, text-to-speech voiceovers, and AI image generation fill other gaps. Some features turn a blog post or product page into a video, which marketers use for repurposing content.

item.title: Flowise
item.description:
Flowise lets people assemble AI applications visually. In its canvas, you connect nodes representing models, prompts, memory, document loaders, vector stores, and tools into a flow, test it in a chat window, and expose it through an API or an embedded widget. It started as a visual layer over LangChain and LlamaIndex and has grown to include agent flows with branching, loops, and human approval steps.

Typical uses include chatbots that answer from company documents, customer support assistants, and agents that call APIs and tools. It supports many model providers, including local models through Ollama, and many vector databases, which gives teams a choice about where data and compute live. Because it is open source, it can be self-hosted, and the project has a strong community and many templates.

item.title: Framer
item.description:
Framer started as a prototyping tool and became a full website builder. Designers lay out pages on a canvas much like they do in Figma, set up responsive behavior, add animations and interactions, and publish to a fast hosted site with a custom domain. Because it gives designers precise control over visuals and motion, it’s popular for portfolios, landing pages, and marketing sites.

A CMS manages blog posts and other structured content, and features for SEO, localization, and analytics support production sites. AI tools generate a first draft of a site from a description, create wireframes, and write copy, which speeds up the start of a project. Components and code overrides allow customization when needed, and a marketplace of templates and plugins helps.

item.title: Gamma
item.description:
Gamma reimagined the presentation. Instead of slides built from a blank template, you describe what you want, such as a pitch for a new product or a lesson on photosynthesis, and Gamma generates a complete, designed deck with text, layouts, and images. The format uses flexible cards that expand and collapse, so presentations can feel more like interactive documents, and it also produces documents and one-page websites.

Editing is conversational and visual. You can ask the AI to rewrite a section, change the style, add images, or restructure, or edit manually with simple controls. Themes keep designs consistent, brand settings apply company fonts and colors, and sharing by link includes analytics on who viewed it. Decks can be exported to PowerPoint or PDF, and it integrates with other tools.

item.title: Imgflip
item.description:
Imgflip makes memes easy. Users pick from a large library of templates, add text, and download or share the result. Other tools on the site include GIF makers, a meme gallery, and custom template uploads, and the community creates and votes on content.

The AI meme generator speeds up the creative step. A user describes a topic or mood, and the tool chooses a template and writes captions, which can then be edited. People use it for social media, group chats, and marketing that leans on humor.

item.title: InVideo
item.description:
InVideo targets creators and marketers who need many videos fast. In InVideo AI, you describe the video you want, such as a product explainer, a faceless YouTube video, or a social ad, and it writes a script, selects stock clips, adds a voiceover and music, and assembles it. You can then give plain-language instructions to change scenes, tone, or length, which makes iteration quick for people without editing skills.

The traditional editor remains for more control. It provides templates, a timeline, text and effects, and a large stock library, and it can turn blog posts and scripts into videos. Voice features include text-to-speech in many languages and voice cloning, and recent versions have added AI-generated video clips and avatars alongside stock footage. Exports are available in formats for different social platforms.

item.title: Kickresume
item.description:
Kickresume helps people create resumes quickly. You choose a template, enter your experience, and the builder arranges everything in a clean layout. A library of professionally designed templates covers different industries and styles, and the exports are designed to be readable by applicant tracking systems, which scan resumes before a human sees them. It also builds cover letters, personal websites, and portfolios.

AI assists with the writing. The AI resume writer can generate summaries and bullet points from your role and achievements, tailor a resume for a specific job description, and write a cover letter. A resume checker evaluates structure, keywords, and clarity and suggests improvements, and extra tools help with interview practice and job tracking. The AI features speed up drafting but can produce generic language.

item.title: LogoAI
item.description:
LogoAI creates logo options from a short brief. A user enters a name, picks an industry and styles they like, and the tool generates a set of designs. They can customize colors, fonts, and layouts, and download vector files and brand assets.

Small businesses and startups use it for a fast start on branding. Packages include business cards, social media graphics, and brand guidelines. The vector output can be used in print and on the web.

item.title: Mematic
item.description:
Mematic makes meme creation quick on a phone. Users pick a template from a large library or upload their own image, add captions in the classic style, and share to social networks and messaging apps. The interface is built for thumb use, so formatting text is fast.

The app offers sticker and filter options, categories of trending templates, and tools for adding emoji and shapes. A premium subscription removes ads and watermarks and adds more templates and features.

item.title: Meme Generator
item.description:
Meme Generator, at memegenerator.net, lets users pick a template, add top and bottom text, and share the result. Its library includes classic image macros and newer formats, and users can upload their own images. A gallery shows popular memes made with the tool.

The AI features help with captions: a user chooses a template and the tool proposes text, which is useful for getting past the blank caption box. Sharing links and downloads are straightforward.

item.title: Mixmax
item.description:
Mixmax turns Gmail into a sales workspace. It tracks opens, clicks, and replies, lets you schedule messages, and adds a calendar tool so recipients can book meetings from your email. Templates and snippets speed up repetitive writing, and polls, surveys, and documents can be embedded. It is used by sales, recruiting, and customer success teams that live in their inbox.

Sequences are a main feature: automated multi-step email campaigns that send follow-ups until someone replies, with rules for pausing and routing. Integrations connect with Salesforce, HubSpot, Outreach alternatives, Slack, and Zapier, so activity is logged in the CRM. AI helps draft emails, personalize at scale, and suggest next steps, and call recording and meeting notes have been added in some plans.

item.title: PandaDoc AI
item.description:
PandaDoc helps sales teams close deals faster. Users build proposals and quotes from templates in a drag-and-drop editor, add pricing tables with live calculations, embed videos and payment links, and send them to clients, who can review and sign electronically. Tracking shows when a document is opened and viewed, so reps know when to follow up.

Automation and integration make it practical for teams. It connects with CRMs like Salesforce and HubSpot to populate documents with deal data and update records when documents are signed, offers approval workflows, content libraries, and a payment step. AI features help generate document content from a prompt, summarize contracts, suggest edits, and extract information, speeding up proposal creation.

item.title: Pitch
item.description:
Pitch aims to make presentations that look good without wrestling with layouts. It provides modern templates, smart slide types, and a brand-aware design system that keeps a team’s decks consistent. Collaboration works like a shared document: several people edit at once, leave comments, and track versions, which suits startups, agencies, and sales teams that produce decks together.

Distinctive features include presentation analytics and sharing. You can send a deck as a link and see who viewed it and for how long, which is helpful for investor and sales decks, and recordings let you narrate a deck for asynchronous sharing. AI tools generate slide drafts from a prompt, rewrite text, and create visuals, and the platform integrates with tools like Slack, HubSpot, and Google Drive.

item.title: Plus AI
item.description:
Plus AI takes the approach that you shouldn’t have to leave your slide editor to use AI. After installing the add-in in Google Slides or PowerPoint, you describe the presentation you want, and it drafts an outline and slides in the editor, which you can then adjust like any other deck. It can also build from a document, a set of notes, or a web page.

Editing features save time on existing decks. The remix tool can restyle or rework slides, and the rewrite function changes tone or length of text on a slide. It can convert content into a different layout, summarize, and create speaker notes. Because the output is native slides, the file remains fully editable and compatible with company templates and brand assets.

item.title: Qwilr
item.description:
Qwilr replaces static PDF proposals with web pages. A seller builds a proposal from blocks, such as text, images, videos, pricing tables, and acceptance sections, and sends a link. Buyers can adjust options in a pricing table, and sign online, which shortens the path to closing.

Analytics show who viewed the page, how long they spent on each section, and when they came back, which guides follow-up. Templates keep branding consistent, and integrations push data into CRMs. AI drafts content from notes and suggests improvements.

item.title: Resume.io
item.description:
Resume.io helps job seekers create a polished resume quickly. You choose a template, fill in your experience, education, and skills in a guided form, and see the layout update. The templates are designed to be clean and readable by applicant tracking systems, and you can adjust colors and fonts, reorder sections, and download the result as a PDF. Cover letter and CV builders follow the same approach.

AI features help with the hard part, which is the wording. The assistant suggests bullet points for a job title, drafts a professional summary, and can tailor a resume to a job description. A resume checker highlights weaknesses, and a job tracker helps manage applications. The tool also provides guides and examples for different professions.

item.title: Slidebean
item.description:
Slidebean separates writing from design. You enter text for each slide in an outline-style editor, choose a slide type such as problem, solution, market, or team, and the software lays it out, selecting fonts, spacing, and graphics so the result looks professional. That means founders can focus on the message and avoid spending hours on layout. AI features help draft slide content and improve wording.

Because it was built for startups, Slidebean adds extras beyond slides. It offers pitch deck templates based on successful funding decks, tools to share decks and see who viewed them, and a financial model builder for projections. The company has also offered pitch deck design and fundraising services for founders who want expert help.

item.title: SlidesAI
item.description:
SlidesAI works inside Google Slides. You paste in text, such as an essay, notes, or an article, or enter a topic, and the add-on creates a set of slides with titles, bullet points, and layout. It lets you pick a presentation style, color theme, and the number of slides, and can add relevant images. The result is a draft that you edit like any other Google Slides deck.

Additional features support content work. It can summarize long text into key points, paraphrase for clarity, and generate text for slides from a prompt. Because the output is a native Slides file, it can be shared, collaborated on, and presented as usual. It’s popular with students, teachers, and professionals who need a quick starting point.

item.title: Supernormal
item.description:
Supernormal aims to make meeting notes require no effort. A bot joins your scheduled meetings, records and transcribes them, and creates notes organized by templates for different types of meetings, such as sales calls, interviews, one-on-ones, and standups. The notes list decisions, action items, and key points, and are shared with attendees or saved to the tools your team uses.

The product works across platforms, including Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams, and also supports in-person meetings. Integrations push notes to Slack, Notion, HubSpot, Salesforce, and Google Docs. Search and chat features let you look back at past meetings and ask questions, and customization options allow you to adjust the format of the notes.

item.title: Tome
item.description:
Tome became a popular early example of generative AI for presentations. A user described a topic, and Tome produced a complete, designed narrative with text, images, and layout, which could be edited in a flexible, canvas-like format. It was positioned as a more modern, storytelling-focused alternative to PowerPoint, and gained millions of users, with attention from students, founders, and professionals.

The company later decided to retire the presentation product and pivot to something different, a sales-focused application. Users were given a period to export their work before the service closed. The pivot reflected a challenge facing many AI tools: general features are quickly matched by larger products, and a standalone app needs a defensible niche.

item.title: Visily
item.description:
Visily is built for people who need to mock up interfaces quickly without learning a full design tool. You can upload a screenshot of an app, a hand-drawn sketch, or a description of a screen, and the AI creates an editable wireframe made of real components. A library of templates, UI kits, and smart components helps assemble screens for web and mobile products.

Collaboration is part of the appeal. Teams can edit together, leave comments, and share clickable prototypes with stakeholders, and designs can be exported or moved into Figma for refinement. Product managers, business analysts, and founders use it to communicate ideas visually and gather feedback early, before engineering work starts.

item.title: Visme AI
item.description:
Visme is aimed at people who need to present information visually without design skills. It offers a drag-and-drop editor with thousands of templates for presentations, infographics, reports, charts, social media posts, and documents. Data widgets create charts and graphs from spreadsheets, and interactive elements such as links and animations can be added. Brand kits keep colors, fonts, and logos consistent across a team.

AI features speed up creation. An AI designer can generate a presentation or document from a prompt, write and rewrite text, create images, and suggest layouts. Teams can collaborate in real time with comments and workflows, and content can be exported as PDF, PowerPoint, or HTML, or shared by link with analytics. Visme is often used by marketers, educators, consultants, and communications teams.

item.title: Wix ADI
item.description:
Wix ADI, short for Artificial Design Intelligence, was an early attempt at automatic site building. A user answered questions about their business and style, and ADI generated a layout with text, images, and a structure suited to the industry. It let people with no design skills get a website online in minutes, long before generative AI was common.

ADI sites had limits. They used a simpler editor than the main Wix Editor, which made it hard to customize them or to add advanced features. Wix has since retired the product: ADI sites are no longer supported and existing ones were moved into the standard Wix Editor, so owners can keep editing them there.

item.title: Writesonic
item.description:
Writesonic started as a template-based copywriter and has widened into a content and marketing suite. Users pick a tool for blog articles, ad copy, product descriptions, emails, or social posts, give a brief, and get a draft. A long-form article writer can produce SEO-minded posts from a keyword with outlines and sources, and a chat assistant answers questions and drafts on demand.

Recent additions center on search visibility. Writesonic has tools to see how a brand is mentioned in AI answer engines such as ChatGPT and Perplexity, plus recommendations for improving content. It also offers brand voice settings, an editor with SEO scoring, and integrations with WordPress and other platforms.

item.title: Writesonic
item.description: Writesonic began as a template-driven AI writer for marketing copy. You choose a type of content, such as a blog post, ad, product description, or social caption, fill in some details, and get a draft. A longer-form article writer builds full posts with an outline, headings, and optional SEO guidance, and a chat assistant answers questions and can search the web. A browser extension and integrations with WordPress and other tools help get content published.

item.title: Zety
item.description: Zety walks job seekers through making a resume. You choose a template, answer prompts about your experience and education, and see a preview that updates as you type. The builder suggests wording for job duties and skills, which is helpful if you struggle with the phrasing, and it formats everything cleanly for PDF or Word download. It also builds cover letters and offers a library of guides and examples for different industries.

item.title: Animoto
item.description:
Animoto was built for people who need a video quickly and do not know editing software. A user uploads photos and video clips, picks a template and a song, and the tool arranges them into a polished video with text and transitions. A storyboard view lets you rearrange scenes and change styles.

It aims at small businesses, real estate agents, educators, and social media marketers. Templates fit common formats such as promos, slideshows, and testimonials, and brand tools apply logos and colors. Videos can be shared online or exported for ads and websites. Newer AI features speed up layout and text creation.

item.title: Vellum
item.description:
Vellum supports teams building AI features for production. Developers and product managers write and compare prompts across models, build workflows that chain steps, and run evaluations against test sets before releasing changes.

Deployment and monitoring tools track versions, costs, and quality, and let teams update prompts without redeploying code. A visual builder and SDK suit both technical and non-technical members.

Vellum has a free tier and paid plans. Alternatives include Langfuse, LangSmith, Braintrust, PromptLayer, and Humanloop, which has shut down. Vellum suits product teams shipping LLM features.

item.title: Adobe Express
item.description:
Adobe Express is Adobe’s answer to Canva: a simple editor where you start from a template, change the text and images, and export. It covers social media posts, banners, flyers, simple videos, and quick edits to PDFs. It runs in the browser and on phones, and it needs no design background. Brand kits, shared templates, and a content scheduler help small teams keep their posts consistent.

The AI tools come from Adobe’s Firefly models. You can generate images from a text prompt, extend or fill parts of a photo, apply text effects from a description, remove backgrounds, and resize a design for several platforms in one step. Because it shares libraries with Creative Cloud, assets from Photoshop or Illustrator can be used directly in Express projects, and designers can hand off a template that colleagues then adjust.

item.title: Dora
item.description:
Dora targets people who want a standout site without writing code. A user describes the site or starts from a template, and the platform generates pages with 3D objects, scroll animations, and interactions, which are expensive to build by hand. A visual editor lets them adjust layout, copy, and motion.

Designers and small businesses use it for portfolios, landing pages, and marketing sites where visual impact matters. Compared with simple builders, it emphasizes motion and depth. Published sites are hosted by the platform, and exporting options vary by plan.

item.title: Fotor
item.description:
Fotor covers everyday editing for people who do not want Photoshop. In the photo editor, you crop, adjust color and light, apply filters and effects, and retouch portraits by smoothing skin and removing blemishes. A collage maker and a design studio offer templates for social posts, posters, and cards. Everything works in a browser, with matching apps for phones and computers.

AI tools handle the harder steps. One-click enhancement improves exposure and sharpness, background removal makes cutouts, an object remover erases distractions, and an upscaler enlarges small pictures. Newer features include text-to-image generation, avatars, and generative fill for extending or changing parts of an image. Fotor also has an AI video editor for simple clips.

item.title: InstaWebAI
item.description:
InstaWebAI generates a full website from a short brief. A user enters information about the business, and the tool creates pages, copy, images, and a structure designed for search engines, which can be edited and published. The goal is to cut the time from idea to live site to minutes.

It targets owners who lack design or writing skills and want a professional baseline. Typical outputs include home, services, about, and contact pages, along with metadata for search visibility. Publishing options and domain connections vary by plan.

item.title: Jason AI
item.description:
Jason AI acts as an automated sales development rep within Reply.io. It finds prospects, writes personalized emails and LinkedIn messages, sends them, and replies to responses to move conversations toward a meeting. It works within Reply.io’s sequencing system, which also handles calls and tasks.

Users give it information about their product and target customers, and Jason builds campaigns. A human can review messages and take over when a lead is interested. The goal is to let small teams reach more prospects without hiring more reps.

item.title: MagicSlides
item.description:
MagicSlides speeds up deck creation. A user enters a topic, pastes text, or uploads a document, and the tool builds slides with titles, bullets, and images. Because it works as an add-on inside Google Slides and PowerPoint, the results land in a familiar editor for refinement.

It supports many languages and offers themes and layouts. Students use it for assignments, and professionals use it to produce a first draft of a presentation, which they then edit. Images can be sourced automatically.

item.title: Rytr
item.description:
Rytr is a simple, affordable writing assistant. You pick a use case, such as a blog section, an ad, a job description, or an email, choose a tone, and give a short brief, and it generates a draft in seconds. It supports many languages and has built-in rewriting and expansion tools, plus a plagiarism checker in higher plans.

The editor resembles a text document, so you can generate content and edit it in one place. Rytr is used by freelancers, small businesses, and students who want quick drafts without learning complex tools, and its price is lower than many competitors. Chrome extensions and an API help use it elsewhere.

item.title: ThumbnailCreator.com
item.description:
ThumbnailCreator targets one chore. A creator describes the thumbnail they want or uploads a frame from a video, and the tool produces several thumbnail options with text, backgrounds, and subjects arranged to catch attention.

Because thumbnails strongly affect click rates, creators iterate on them often. A generator that makes variations lets them test ideas without opening a design program each time.

Independent information is limited. ThumbnailCreator has a free tier and paid plans. Alternatives include Canva, Photoroom, VidIQ and TubeBuddy thumbnail tools, Midjourney, and hiring a designer. ThumbnailCreator suits YouTubers who make many thumbnails.
